facts.statement: Andalgalornis was a flightless predatory bird belonging to the extinct family Phorusrhacidae, commonly known as terror birds, that lived in Argentina.
facts.quote: Andalgalornis is a genus of flightless predatory birds of the extinct family Phorusrhacidae (often called "terror birds") that lived in Argentina.

facts.statement: The only known species of the genus Andalgalornis is A. steulleti.
facts.quote: The type and only species is A. steulleti.

facts.statement: Fossils of Andalgalornis include an incomplete skeleton and isolated bones found in the Entre Ríos and Catamarca Provinces of Argentina.
facts.quote: Andalgalornis is known from an incomplete skeleton and some single bones found from sites in the Entre Ríos and Catamarca Provinces of northeast and northwest Argentina.

facts.statement: Andalgalornis fossils were discovered in the Late Miocene Ituzaingó Formation within the Paraná Basin.
facts.quote: The fossils were uncovered from the Late Miocene (Huayquerian in the SALMA classification) Ituzaingó Formation of the Paraná Basin.

facts.statement: Andalgalornis stood approximately 1.4 meters tall and weighed about 40 kilograms.
facts.quote: Around 1.4 m tall in height, Andalgalornis is estimated to have weighed around 40 kg, on the basis of the methodology proposed by Campbell and Marcus (1992).

facts.statement: Andalgalornis resembled the larger Phorusrhacos but was more elegant, smaller, and possessed the most massive beak relative to its body size among all phorusrhacids.
facts.quote: it looked much like the larger phorusrhacid Phorusrhacos, but it was more elegant and smaller and had a proportionally higher beak, the most massive in proportion to body size of all phorusrhacids.

facts.statement: Research suggests Andalgalornis had a skull adapted for rigidity, showing high stress under sideways loads but low stress when force was applied vertically or during pullback simulations.
facts.quote: These researchers interpreted this loss as an adaptation for enhanced rigidity of the skull, and compared to the modern red-legged seriema and white-tailed eagle, the skull of the phorusrhacid showed relatively high stress under sideways loadings, but low stress where force was applied up and down, and in simulations of "pullback".

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Andalgalornis likely fed on small prey or used an "attack-and-retreat" strategy with repetitive strikes against larger prey rather than subduing them directly.
facts.quote: Instead, they suggested that it either fed on smaller prey that could be killed and consumed more safely, by, for example, swallowing it whole, or that when targeting large prey, it used a series of well-targeted repetitive strikes with the beak, in an "attack-and-retreat" strategy.

facts.statement: A 2012 study found that the neck of Andalgalornis was divided into three sections and adapted for carrying a large head and rising after a downward strike.
facts.quote: A 2012 follow-up study by Tambussi and colleagues analyzed the flexion abilities of the neck of Andalgalornis, based on the morphology of its neck vertebrae, finding the neck to be divided into three sections.

facts.statement: A 2020 study classified Andalgalornis as belonging to the "Terror Bird Skull Type," a specialized morphotype characterized by rigid and stiff skulls derived from a seriema-like ancestor.
facts.quote: A 2020 study of phorusrhacid skull morphology by Degrange found that there were two main morphotypes within the group, derived from a seriema-like ancestor; the "Psilopterine Skull Type", which was plesiomorphic (more similar to the ancestral type), and the "Terror Bird Skull Type", which included Andalgalornis and other large members, that was more specialized, with more rigid and stiff skulls.

facts.statement: Andalgalornis fossils date from 7 to 5 million years ago and were found in the Andalhuala Formation in the Santa María Valley of Catamarca Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Andalgalornis es conocida a partir de un esqueleto incompleto y algunos huesos aislados encontrados en estratos sedimentarios terciarios del Mioceno Superior al Plioceno Inferior y correspondiente a una edad geológica entre 7 a 5 millones de años (pertenecientes a la Formación Andalhuala, de sitio en la villa de Chiquimil, localidad de Entre Ríos, valle de Santa María, provincia de Catamarca, en el noroeste de Argentina.

facts.statement: The fossils were recovered in April 1926 by a US paleontological expedition led by geologist Germán Young and collector Rudolf Stahlecker, assisted by local guides Juan and Felipe Méndez.
facts.quote: Estos fueron recuperados por una expedición paleontológica realizada por un grupo de científicos de Estados Unidos en abril de 1926, el campamento estuvo integrado por Germán Young (geólogo), Rudolf Stahlecker (recolector) y dos nativos de la región: Juan y Felipe Méndez

facts.statement: Andalgalornis measured 1.4 meters in height, had a 37 cm head, and is thought to have preyed on small rodent-like mammals such as Paedotherium.
facts.quote: Esta ave medía 1,4 metros de altura y tenía una enorme cabeza de 37cm y se alimentaba de mamíferos pequeños parecidos a roedores como el Paedotherium.

facts.statement: CT scans suggest Andalgalornis had a beak that was strong vertically but relatively weak laterally.
facts.quote: Un análisis realizado con escáner TAC del cráneo de Andalgalornis sugiere que el pico era fuerte en sentido dorsoventral (es decir, en el plano vertical) pero en cambio era relativamente débil mediolateralmente (a los lados).

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the strong vertical beak of Andalgalornis may have allowed it to quickly strike prey using a repetitive attack-and-retreat hunting strategy.
facts.quote: Aun así, el que el pico fuera fuerte dorsoventralmente le pudo haber permitido a Andalgalornis abatir con rapidez a una presa con una estrategia de caza consistente en atacar y retirarse de manera repetida.

facts.statement: A study of the neck vertebrae indicated they were structurally adapted for striking.
facts.quote: Un estudio de sus vértebras del cuello mostró que estas estaban constituidas para golpear.

facts.statement: Andalgalornis is classified in the order Cariamiformes and family Phorusrhacidae, with the genus authority cited as Patterson & Kraglievich, 1960.

facts.statement: Andalgalornis has several synonyms, including Phororhacos steulleti, Phororhacos deautieri, Andalgalornis ferox, and Phorohacos deautieri.
facts.quote: synonyms: Phororhacos steulleti Kraglievich, 1931 Phororhacos deautieri Kraglievich, 1931 Andalgalornis ferox Patterson & Kraglievich, 1960 Phorohacos deautieri Kraglievich, 1931

facts.statement: The time range for the genus Andalgalornis is estimated from 8 to 5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Zanclean (8 to 5 million years ago)
